Contributing to rfm

Source: .github/CONTRIBUTING.md

Thanks for helping improve rfm. This guide covers bug reports, fixes, and pull requests.

Reporting a bug

  • Search existing issues before opening a new one.
  • Every issue must include a reproducible example (a “reprex”). Use the bug report form and keep the example minimal. Build it with reprex: library(rfm), a small inline data frame or a built-in dataset, the call, and its output.
  • Include the full error or warning text, your sessionInfo() output, and the package version and install source (CRAN or a GitHub commit).
  • Confirm the example fails in a fresh R session.

How fixes are verified

Every fixing pull request adds a test built from the issue’s example. Before the issue is closed, the maintainer re-runs that example on the fix and posts the output in the closing comment, together with the commit or pull request.

Proposing a change

Open an issue first for anything beyond a typo or a small documentation fix. Explain the problem and, for a new feature, show the proposed interface with an example call and the alternatives you considered.

Pull requests

  • Branch from develop. master is only for releases.
  • Add a bullet to NEWS.md describing the change.
  • Add tests with testthat.
  • Run devtools::check(); it should finish with no errors or warnings.
  • Follow the tidyverse style guide.

Code of conduct

This project is released with a Contributor Code of Conduct. By participating, you agree to abide by its terms.
